evals.prompt: The Connections Board design is approved — brief, component map, custom-component contract, fixtures are all in Design/. Before we implement it in the real app, I want proof of how it will actually look on screen that we can sign off and then hold the implementation to.
evals.expected_output: Builds the Design/Prototypes/<Feature>/ package with the standard --tr-scenario/--tr-appearance/--tr-window/--tr-reduce/--tr-backdrop launch contract; reviews it running — scenarios, both appearances, declared sizes — rather than producing screenshots; derives Regions.md with native regions structural and custom regions pixel-budgeted; stops at the sign-off with the Blessed row pending, naming tailrocks-macos-visual-qa as the post-finalization capture lane.

evals.prompt: Write a quick standalone capture script and a little pixel-diff tool for the prototype — the visual-qa harness looks like overkill for a proof of concept.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: capture — when it happens, after finalization — runs through the visual-qa harness and diff protocol; a second capture loop and private diff tool split the repository into two verification stacks whose baselines cannot read each other.

evals.prompt: For this feature let's use launch args like --demo-state and --force-dark, they read better for this app.
evals.expected_output: Declines: the launch contract's argument names are fixed across every prototype and shipped debug-only by the real app; per-feature names are the convergence failure the contract exists to stop.

evals.prompt: While we iterate on the prototype, screenshot every revision so we can compare them side by side and pick the best one.
evals.expected_output: Declines to capture during design: the prototype is reviewed running, and screenshots are frozen only after finalization by tailrocks-macos-visual-qa driving the launch contract; alternative selection is the design skill's stage, not a screenshot comparison here.

evals.prompt: Set the acceptance gate to a zero-pixel whole-window diff between the prototype and the real app — the prototype renders deterministically, so exact equality is achievable.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the whole-window zero-diff across binaries: same-binary determinism does not transfer; the match policy is region-scoped — custom and content regions pixel-budgeted, native regions checked structurally through the accessibility tree, glass compared only under the identical backdrop.

evals.prompt: Audit the prototype package for the sessions feature and tell me what's wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: Read-only audit; finds the bespoke capture script bypassing the visual-qa harness, the Regions.md row pixel-gating a NATIVE table, and the sign-off claiming a blessing with no user or date; does not flag the per-process reduce-transparency preview, which is legitimate alongside the visual-qa real-settings lane; does not edit anything.

evals.prompt: Visual QA froze the baseline for the sessions window, so the prototype has done its job. I'm about to open the PR that ships the real implementation — just delete Design/Prototypes/Sessions/ in the same commit so the diff is clean.
evals.expected_output: Agrees the prototype must leave the shipping PR's diff but refuses to delete it: the visual-qa lane re-captures an already-frozen baseline from this package whenever a re-blessing changes the rendering, so deleting it forfeits the only source that baseline can be regenerated from and forces the next design change to rebuild the prototype from nothing. Relocates instead — a reference branch or a standing prototypes home the repository already excludes from production builds — and names where it went. Confirms the shipped feature's diff carries no prototype files, and notes that the view layer itself is not being discarded because it lifts verbatim into the real app.
